concept.name: Operating margin
concept.definition: Income from operations as a percentage of net revenues - the share of each sales dollar left after production costs and operating expenses, but before interest and taxes. The SEC's investors' guide defines it exactly as income from operations divided by net revenues.
concept.intuition: It captures the profitability of the core business itself, independent of how the company is financed or taxed.
concept.mechanics: From the income statement, take operating income (gross profit minus selling, general and administrative costs, R&D, and depreciation and amortization) and divide by net revenue; because it excludes interest and taxes it is often called the EBIT margin.
concept.formula: Operating margin = Income from operations / Net revenues x 100.
concept.failure_modes: 'Operating' definitions vary - some firms exclude restructuring or stock-based compensation - so adjusted margins across vendors are not always comparable, and the metric hides the interest burden of leveraged firms.
concept.misconceptions: A healthy operating margin does not guarantee survival: debt service and capital expenditure live below the operating line, and a margin percentage says nothing about absolute profit dollars.
concept.example: With $50 million of operating income on $200 million of net revenue, operating margin is 25% - each sales dollar yields 25 cents of profit before interest and taxes.

citations.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Beginners' Guide to Financial Statements
